quote: Solar is just a scam, but I appreciate your call.
stewart_read: This is a textbook trust_or_scam objection; the rep had a flip available (e.g., reframe the ZIP-code form as the customer's own initiated action) and instead skipped straight to an unrelated qualifying question.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic deferral is not supported — there's no later moment where the rep returns to address the scam claim, so this reads as a missed handling, not a deliberate hold.
coaching_implication: Rep should acknowledge the scam concern directly and specifically (per protocols on legitimacy) before pivoting elsewhere; silence on it lets the suspicion calcify.

quote: Well, do you already have solar, Carol?
stewart_read: Good instinct to check for existing solar, but the rep gets a 'Yes' and does not follow the orphaned_flow script (owned/leased, company, working status) before the call ends.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive — the rep asked to buy time after the scam comment rather than as a planned qualification step, evidenced by the abrupt, unscripted phrasing 'Well, do you already have solar.'
coaching_implication: Once existing solar surfaces, immediately run orphaned_flow: ownership, installer, system health. That's the only viable path left on this call and it was skipped.

quote: And do we use Solar Energy World, Frank? We use Solar Energy World.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers the name of her existing installer, a valuable competitive data point, and the rep does not capture it or ask a single follow-up.
coaching_implication: Even on a lost call, capturing competitor name and system status has floor-wide value; rep should have asked 'is it working well for you?' or similar before disengaging.

quote: Yes. It makes sense, but I'm not interested because I think we have what we're supposed to have, and we're good.
stewart_read: This is a not_interested / already_have_system objection; canonical rebuttal strategy (curiosity_creation, comparison_framing) was available and unused.
alternative_hypothesis: Not strategic — the rep's very next line is a full concession, with no attempt at even a single-angle rebuttal.
coaching_implication: Use comparison_framing: 'it's worth a second look to compare pricing/equipment against what you have' even on an existing-system lead.

quote: So this is Holland with Ion. I got a request that Carol was looking into solar for her home
stewart_read: Rep establishes company name and references the lead source reasonably well, which is a partial legitimacy anchor, but doesn't mention the form/site specifically until the customer surfaces her own suspicion about the ZIP-code site.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be adequate — the rep does reference 'a request' as the source, which is a legitimacy anchor, so this may not be a true omission.
coaching_implication: Front-load the specific lead source ('the solar interest form you filled out') rather than the vaguer 'a request' to preempt the scam suspicion that surfaces 30 seconds later.

quote: Okay? Okay. No problem. Have a good one.
stewart_read: Call ends with no next step, no attempt to leave a door open (e.g., offer to text info, or note for future follow-up), a flat concession exit.
coaching_implication: Even on a hard decline, closing with a soft door-opener costs nothing and preserves future contact value.
